Independent check: Co is +3, so it is d⁶. F⁻ is weak-field; octahedral Co(III) is high-spin with 4 unpaired electrons. Thus μ = √[4(4+2)] = √24 BM.
solution:
For $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$, cobalt is in the $+3$ oxidation state, so $\text{Co}^{3+}$ is $3d^6$. Since $\text{F}^-$ is a weak-field ligand, the complex is high-spin with $n=4$ unpaired electrons.
$$\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=\sqrt{4(4+2)}=\sqrt{24}\ \text{BM}$$
